correctness.rationale: The explicit potential differentiates to z-1/b+(y-bx)^2/(ab), verified exactly by the packaged SymPy checker; subtraction from ordinary divergence z-b yields weighted divergence 1/b-b-(y-bx)^2/(ab). Liouville identity follows for each flow segment; bounded potential on compact invariant K transfers uniform exponential rate to Euclidean determinant. Integration of an exact generator coboundary against a compact invariant probability is zero. Equality forces xdot=0 on entire orbits by invariance/continuity, whose only compact complete solutions are E±; mixtures exactly attain bound. Oseledets sums equal integrated divergence on compact ergodic supports. At equilibria the rate 1/b-b is exact, so threshold and exponential constant are optimal.

originality.rationale: Sprott (2014, Eq. 6) first states this exact damped oscillator, and Munmuangsaen et al. (2015, Sec. 2) gives a numerical attractor dimension/trace analysis. Neither inspected primary text asserts the quadratic cohomological cancellation, globally sign-definite weighted divergence, optimal b=1 boundary or equality rigidity across all compact invariant measures. Other known weighted-volume results concern distinct vector fields. Searches and close implication comparisons are recorded below. Residual risk is genuine but not decisive: unindexed older calculations might exist.
residual_risks: Historical or unindexed unpublished derivations of a similar Gaussian weight could be missed; nonappearance in searched literature cannot establish universal novelty.

value.rationale: The exact same two-parameter oscillator underlies published investigations of linked chaotic attractors, attractor merging, numerical Lyapunov sums and adjustable dimension. Its ordinary divergence z-b has indefinite sign over phase space; a non-obvious explicit quadratic cohomology creates a sharp global damping-controlled weighted-volume frontier, exact optimal finite-time contraction on compact invariant sets and equality-rigid Lyapunov sum bound for every compact stationary state. These global statements cannot be obtained from an equilibrium trace or finite parameter samples and have an intrinsic role in comparing distinct recurrent regimes. Limits: weighted density is not a global probability and chaotic-set existence is not implied.
